pr_comments: looks fine can you add a whatsnew note

Certainly no objection to the modification here, but I do wonder if we should be changing the API to narrow what is allowed as a Series name or DataFrame label. For example, from #39757,
```
series_a = Series([1,2,3], name=np.float64(1.0))
series_b = Series([1,2,3], name=(np.float64(1.0), np.float64(2.0)))
pd.concat([series_a, series_b], axis=1).columns.sort_values()
```

still fails. I am wondering if we should change the API to only allow basic primitive types (Boolean, int, str, float?, perhaps some others) and tuples of primitive types, rather than trying to chase these issues down.
the problem is that the name can be any pandas primitive or tuplr if those (as we allow this for index labels) which doesn't it much
@jreback - I think you're saying that even if we were to add some restrictions, `np.float64` (and hence, tuples of such objects) should be allowed as a name. Is that right?
yes ultimately we allow these as names (well have to be hashable) or we could inhibit a number of downstream ops

issue_context.title: ValueError from operations between Series with specific names
issue_context.body:
The following raises a ValueError due to comparison of the two names in the function _maybe_match_name (core/ops/common.py).

```python
>>> from pandas import Series
>>> import numpy as np
>>> series_a = Series([1,2,3], name=np.float64(1.0))
>>> series_b = Series([1,2,3], name=(np.float64(1.0), np.float64(2.0)))
>>> series_a + series_b
```

It seems to only occur when comparison a tuple of numpy dtypes to a single numpy dtype, but I didn't test every possible combination. It does not occur when using built-in floats, I imagine this is due to overloading of the == operator by the numpy dtypes when the other operand is a tuple.

There is a nearby TODO "what if they both have np.nan for their names?" I don't know how feasible it is to consider every case where equality fails, but it seems a try/except returning None would seem to resolve this issue, and be in line with the default return value if the names do not compare equal. I would be keen to implement this simple fix if it seems sensible.

comments:
Thanks for the report! From https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.Series.html:

> name: str, optional

Certainly other types (integers) need to be allowed, but I wonder how much of pandas also depends on the name being comparable. An alternative would be to add this requirement.

It seems to me that None is the default output when a name cannot be reasonably deduced, and so a try/except block could be a clean fix, if not a permanent design choice. Series with tuple-type names can arise naturally when accessing a DataFrame with multi-level columns for example.
@dan1261 - I think this issue is not the presence of tuples but rather numpy objects. Tuples are comparable (edit: assuming their components are).

@rhshadrach indeed it seems the only problem is a comparison of a numpy object with a tuple of numpy objects. Just wanted to highlight that tuples of such objects can occur naturally. I believe the try/except fix should work in any case

@dan1261 - In this case yes, but other methods fail, e.g.:

```
series_a = Series([1,2,3], name=np.float64(1.0))
series_b = Series([1,2,3], name=(np.float64(1.0), np.float64(2.0)))
pd.concat([series_a, series_b], axis=1).columns.sort_values()
```

raises

```
File "pandas/pandas/pandas/core/sorting.py", line 385, in nargsort
    indexer = non_nan_idx[non_nans.argsort(kind=kind)]
```

which would also need to be fixed. It seems to me trying to support such objects is opening a can of worms.
